questions.stem: Part 4 of the Small Vessel Regulations applies to which vessels?
options: Any vessel under 24 m in length that carries people
Any fishing vessel of not more than 15 gross tonnage
Any passenger vessel, whatever its size or tonnage
Passenger vessels of 15 GT or less carrying 12 or fewer passengers
questions.explanation: Section 400(1) sets those limits; above either number the vessel goes into the inspection certificate regime. Fishing vessels are excluded from the Regulations altogether by s. 2(2).

questions.stem: Before leaving the place where passengers embark, what must the operator include with the safety briefing?
options: A written test on the briefing for each passenger aboard
A demonstration of how to don each type of lifejacket
A signed waiver from every passenger on board
A demonstration of the vessel's radar and GPS
questions.explanation: Section 401(2) requires a donning demonstration for each type of lifejacket during the briefing. Tests, waivers and radar demonstrations are not required.

questions.stem: What must an operator do before departure about the number of persons on board?
options: Report it to the Minister of Transport for each trip
Report it to a designated person ashore who can contact search and rescue
Write it on the dock sign-in sheet and leave it there
Nothing, if the trip is shorter than one hour
questions.explanation: Section 402(1) requires the report to a designated person ashore. If the vessel works in a remote area where that is impossible, the information is left at a known location ashore (s. 402(2)).

questions.stem: A water taxi carries no life raft and the water temperature is 9 degrees C. What does s. 403 require?
options: Nothing, because the vessel is small and the trips are short
Carry equipment or set procedures to protect against hypothermia and cold shock
Passengers must wear immersion suits at all times when under way
A life raft must be added before the next trip, whatever the season
questions.explanation: Section 403 applies below 15 degrees C when there is no life raft, and it allows equipment or procedures, not necessarily a life raft or suits.

questions.stem: A 7.5 m passenger-carrying vessel needs visual signals. Which is correct?
options: A watertight flashlight and three pyrotechnic distress signals
A watertight flashlight and six pyrotechnic distress signals other than smoke signals
Six pyrotechnic distress signals and no flashlight
A watertight flashlight and twelve pyrotechnic distress signals, up to six of which may be smoke
questions.explanation: Section 410 gives 3 up to 6 m, 6 for over 6 m to 9 m (no smoke), and 12 over 9 m (not more than 6 smoke). A flashlight is required in all three bands.

questions.stem: A hand flare was manufactured on March 1, 2022 and purchased new on May 1, 2022. When does it expire under s. 20?
options: It does not expire as long as the case is unopened
Four years after purchase, on May 1, 2026
Four years after manufacture, on March 1, 2026
Three years after manufacture, on March 1, 2025
questions.explanation: Section 20(1) counts four years from the date of manufacture, not purchase, and does not exempt unopened ones.

questions.stem: Which vessel is NOT required by s. 411 to carry a life raft with capacity for everyone on board?
options: A 10 m passenger vessel on a near coastal voyage, Class 2, 20 nautical miles offshore
A 10 m passenger vessel on a sheltered waters voyage
A 12 m passenger vessel on a voyage beyond sheltered waters, far from any river or lake shore
An 11 m passenger vessel on a near coastal voyage, Class 2
questions.explanation: Section 411(2) exempts a vessel that is not more than 8.5 m, on a sheltered waters voyage, or within 2 nautical miles of the shore of a river or lake. The 10 m vessel on a sheltered voyage qualifies; the others do not.

questions.stem: How much anchor rode (cable, rope or chain) must an 11 m passenger vessel carry under s. 412?
options: At least 15 m
None, if she has a manual propelling device
At least 30 m
At least 50 m
questions.explanation: Over 9 m to 12 m, the table requires an anchor with at least 30 m and a manual bilge pump. The 15 m figure is up to 9 m, 50 m is over 12 m, and the manual propelling alternative exists only in the up to 9 m band.

questions.stem: Which portable extinguisher fits a 7 m passenger vessel with no cooking appliance under s. 414?
options: A 2A:10B:C extinguisher, plus a 10B:C at the engine space
A single 2A:20B:C extinguisher at the helm only
A single 1A:5B:C extinguisher at the helm only
A single 10B:C extinguisher at the engine space entrance only
questions.explanation: Over 6 m to 9 m requires a 2A:10B:C and a 10B:C at the engine space entrance; the single 1A:5B:C is up to 6 m, and 2A:20B:C applies over 12 m.

questions.stem: A 5.8 m passenger boat has an enclosed engine space. Which detector does s. 418 require in the engine space?
options: A smoke detector with its own battery and a 60 dB alarm in the main cabin
A fixed CO2 system in every case, whatever the size of the space
No detector, because the vessel is under 6 m and has an outboard
A heat detector with visual and audible alarms at the operating position
questions.explanation: Section 418(1)(a) requires that heat detector in each engine space for a vessel of 6 m or less, unless the engine is enclosed so that a fire would be immediately apparent at the operating position (s. 418(2)).

questions.stem: What quantity of carbon dioxide must a portable extinguisher intended for direct discharge into an enclosed engine space contain, and how fast must it discharge?
options: 1.2 kg per cubic metre of gross volume, discharged in 60 seconds or less
1.2 kg per cubic metre, discharged in not more than 10 seconds
12 kg per cubic metre of net volume, discharged in about 60 seconds or less
0.6 kg per cubic metre of gross volume, discharged over 2 minutes
questions.explanation: Section 416 gives 1.2 kg per cubic metre and 60 seconds for CO2; a clean agent must provide equivalent protection and discharge in not more than 10 seconds.

questions.stem: How long must the engine space blower run before a gasoline-powered vessel's engine is started?
options: Not less than four minutes immediately before starting
Not less than 30 seconds, or until the fumes smell clear
Not less than ten minutes on every occasion
Only if the engine fails to start the first time
questions.explanation: Section 1001 sets four minutes of blower operation immediately before starting a gasoline-powered vessel.

questions.stem: What must the owner of a passenger-carrying vessel do before the vessel is first put in service?
options: Obtain an inspection certificate from a marine safety inspector
Tell the Minister of the intended operation and the vessel's details
Register the vessel's flares and lifejackets with the Canadian Coast Guard
Obtain written approval of every passenger list from the Minister
questions.explanation: Section 405 requires that notice to the Minister before first service. An inspection certificate is a different regime that applies above 15 GT or 12 passengers.

questions.stem: A 9.5 m passenger vessel must carry throwing gear. Which choice meets s. 409?
options: A lifebuoy with a self-igniting light, and nothing else
A 15 m buoyant heaving line and a lifebuoy on a 15 m buoyant line
A buoyant heaving line of at least 15 m, and nothing else
A lifebuoy attached to a buoyant line of at least 15 m, and nothing else
questions.explanation: Over 9 m to 12 m the table requires both items. The either-or choice applies over 6 m to 9 m, and the lifebuoy with a self-igniting light (or on a buoyant line) applies over 12 m.

questions.stem: On a passenger boat, who must be given an inherently buoyant lifejacket, and when is a reboarding device not required?
options: Anyone under 12; a reboarding device is not required if the vessel is under 15 GT
Anyone under 16; no reboarding device if the climb is 0.5 m or less
Only the crew; a reboarding device is never required on passenger boats
Anyone over 65; a reboarding device is not required on vessels under 12 m
questions.explanation: Section 408 requires inherently buoyant lifejackets for persons under 16, and s. 409(1)(b) requires a reboarding device unless the vertical height to be climbed is not more than 0.5 m.
